item.title: Xi extends condolences over death of Japan's former PM Yasuo Fukuda
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday extended condolences over the death of former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda to his family. In his message, Xi also extended sympathy to the family. Fukuda was a Japanese statesman known for his integrity and sense of responsibility, as well as a longtime friend of the Chinese people. He had long been committed to the China-Japan friendship and upheld a correct view of history, Xi said. During his tenure as prime minister, he signed the fourth political document between China and Japan with the Chinese side, setting out important principles for the development of bilateral relations, Xi said. Fukuda also served as chairman of the Boao Forum for Asia, playing an important role in promoting exchanges and cooperation in Asia, Xi said, noting that China will remember his contributions to China-Japan relations and Asia's development. Xi also expressed the hope that Fukuda's family would carry on his legacy and continue to work for China-Japan friendship. Xi expressed the hope that Japanese authorities would cherish the efforts of previous generations of statesmen, abide by the four political documents between China and Japan, and safeguard the political foundation of bilateral relations.

item.title: Xi congratulates Lula on re-election as Brazilian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday extended congratulations to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election as president of Brazil. In his congratulatory message, Xi said that President Lula has made important contributions to advancing China-Brazil relations. Xi said he and Lula have, in recent years, maintained close communication through various means and jointly guided the building of the China-Brazil community with a shared future for a more just world and a more sustainable planet to new progress. The global, strategic and long-term significance of the bilateral relationship has become increasingly prominent, making it a model of solidarity and cooperation among Global South countries, he said. Xi said that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Brazil relations and stands ready to work with President Lula to guide the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future to new heights, open up broader prospects for all-round strategic coordination between the two countries, and continuously enhance the well-being of the two peoples. Also on Tuesday, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng sent a congratulatory message to Geraldo Alckmin on his re-election as Brazil's vice president.

item.title: China issues regulation on registration, management of public institutions
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
BEIJING, Oct. 26 -- China has issued a regulation on the registration and management of public institutions, aiming to strengthen the Party's overall leadership over such institutions and reinforce their commitment to serving the public interest. Premier Li Qiang signed a State Council decree promulgating the regulation, which consists of six chapters and 34 articles and will take effect on Dec. 1. The regulation also standardizes registration and management procedures and safeguards public institutions' legitimate rights and interests. It requires public institutions to uphold the leadership of the Communist Party of China, firmly implement the Party's lines, principles and policies, and step up efforts to improve conduct, enforce discipline and combat corruption. It also calls on public institutions to remain committed to serving the public interest, prioritize social benefits, and continuously improve the quality and efficiency of their public services. The regulation further stipulates that competent authorities and sponsoring organizations must oversee and guide public institutions to ensure their activities are conducted in accordance with the law. Industry regulators, including those in the medical, educational and scientific research sectors, are also required to strengthen supervision and inspections of relevant institutions' conduct. To improve registration services, the regulation calls for standardized and streamlined procedures. Registration authorities and public institutions are required to promptly disclose relevant information through the national public institution registration and management information platform, in accordance with the law.

item.title: Xi leads CPC to advance full, rigorous self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
BEIJING, Oct. 26 -- The Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee on Monday started a four-day plenary session in Beijing, which focuses on strengthening Party self-governance. This marks the latest move by the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core to strengthen the Party through full and rigorous self-governance. Xi, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, has emphasized that exercising full and rigorous self-governance is an enduring task for the Party. "One has to be very strong if he wants to strike the iron," Xi said shortly after his election to the post of general secretary of the CPC Central Committee in November 2012. He later warned at a group study session of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee that if corruption is allowed to grow unchecked, "it could spell the end of both the Party and the state." As China entered the new era, the CPC, the largest governing party in the world, faced unprecedented challenges in ensuring reform, development and stability, and addressing problems and risks confronting the nation. Xi has stressed that China's success hinges on the Party, and has made clear that the CPC must continuously strengthen itself through self-governance. In 2014, he explicitly put forward the concept of "exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance" as part of the Party's four-pronged governing strategy, alongside building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, deepening reform and advancing law-based governance. He has made full and rigorous Party self-governance a long-term strategy, as he considers it vital to the Party's long-term governance, the country's enduring stability, and the people's happiness and well-being. BREAK NEW GROUND In December 2012, Xi began strengthening Party self-governance by introducing a code of conduct that became known as the "eight-point rules." It established regulations for Party leaders regarding research tours, meetings, documentation, and other official duties, cracking down on lavish banquets, red carpet events, pomp, entourages, unnecessary meetings, and luxury perks that had once been regarded by some as typical symbols of power. Its implementation has helped curb longstanding malpractices, with effects extending beyond Party and government offices to wider society. "The eight-point rules have indeed brought about fundamental changes over the years," Xi said last year, when the Party launched a campaign to reinforce this code of conduct and consolidate the improvements it had brought about. Xi also launched an unprecedented anti-corruption storm that has swept every corner of public office, netting both high-ranking "tigers" and lower-level "flies." Some of the most senior officials -- including former members of the Political Bureau and its Standing Committee, top military brass, and retirees who left their leading positions years ago -- have been brought to justice. The anti-corruption campaign has continued unabated, with Xi stressing that the fight is an ongoing endeavor. In 2025 alone, 115 officials at ministerial level or above were placed under investigation, while 627,000 people were disciplined in cases involving misconduct and corruption that affect the people's immediate interests. The same year, China also opened investigations into more than 500 cases of cross-border corruption. At a plenary session of the CPC's top disciplinary body early this year, Xi again warned that corruption remains a problem that arises all too easily and frequently. "We must see the fight against corruption through to the end, no matter how great the resistance or how high the cost," he said. "No one who engages in corruption will be shown leniency, regardless of who they are, how high their rank or how great their contributions." EFFECTIVE APPROACHES To strengthen full and rigorous Party self-governance, it is imperative to uphold the Party's overall leadership. Over the past 14 years, the Party's leadership has been further affirmed in both the Party Constitution and the country's Constitution. Central commissions have been established to oversee key areas including reform, national security, cyberspace affairs, and financial and economic affairs. Working mechanisms for central decision-making and coordinating bodies have also been strengthened. Strengthening theoretical education is another approach. With Xi at the helm, the CPC has launched nine Party-wide major education campaigns. The latest one, launched in February this year, prodded Party members to fix their mindset regarding governance performance, aiming to stamp out the tendency among some officials to sacrifice public well-being in seeking to polish their performance records. This campaign built on the gains of previous ones on Party discipline and implementing the eight-point rules, among others, to advance the Party's self-governance. These efforts have gone hand in hand with institution-building. Under Xi's watch, the Party and state oversight systems have been improved. The National Commission of Supervision and local supervisory commissions were established to bring everyone in public office, regardless of Party membership, under supervision. And Xi has made discipline inspections a key instrument of intra-Party oversight. The inspection system allows higher-level Party authorities to send teams to examine how officials exercise power and carry out the central leadership's policies. Inspectors interview officials and members of the public, review documents and receive complaints. They report their findings to Party authorities. After each round of inspections launched by the Party Central Committee, Xi reviewed the reports in detail, assessed the problems uncovered and pushed for further improvements in inspection work. Since 2012, the Party has also formulated or revised an unprecedented number of internal regulations, building a comprehensive framework of rules to confine power in "a cage of institutions." Noting the progress, Xi also warned that in some localities, rules were poorly enforced while "hidden rules" prevailed. He stressed that regulations must become "high-voltage lines" and that power must be exercised transparently, leaving no room for such hidden rules. All these mechanisms are part of the integrated efforts to ensure officials, in Xi's words, "do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to become corrupt." LEADING MODERNIZATION DRIVE Full and rigorous Party self-governance serves a broader purpose: strengthening the Party's capacity to lead China's modernization drive. "To successfully achieve the goals and tasks of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), it is imperative to focus on enhancing the ability and competence of the Party in leading economic and social development," Xi told senior provincial- and ministerial-level officials attending a study session at the Party School of the CPC Central Committee earlier this year. He urged Party officials to become more capable of pursuing high-quality development, serving the people, and guarding against and defusing risks. China has entered a critical period for achieving the goal of basically realizing modernization by 2035, and still faces rising uncertainty abroad and mounting challenges at home. At such critical junctures, strong Party leadership is vital to chart the course. All Party members, Xi said, must remain true to the Party's original aspiration and mission, and lead the nation to "create new historic glories."

item.title: 20th CPC Central Committee starts fifth plenary session
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
BEIJING, Oct. 26 -- The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) started its fifth plenary session in Beijing on Monday morning. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a work report on behalf of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and expounded on a draft decision of the CPC Central Committee on some major issues concerning strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance. The draft decision summarizes the achievements and experience of full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era in a truth-seeking manner, and offers in-depth analysis of the situation and tasks concerning Party building at present and for some time to come. It also sets out strategic plans for strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance, according to a Political Bureau meeting in September that decided to submit the document to the plenum for review. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the full and rigorous Party self-governance has made significant progress, opened up a new frontier for the century-old Party in self-reform, and brought about historic achievements and transformations in the cause of the Party and the country, said an earlier Political Bureau meeting in July that set the plenum's agenda. The meeting said the Party and the people have won the historical initiative to build a strong Party and country, but noted that as profound changes unfold in the world, in China and within the Party, efforts to exercise full and rigorous Party self-governance also face many new circumstances and challenges. It called for adopting higher standards and taking more concrete measures to uphold and apply the valuable experience of full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era, resolve the prominent issues facing Party building, and consolidate and develop the sound political environment created through Party self-supervision and self-governance.

item.title: Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
BEIJING, Oct. 23 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday presided over a State Council executive meeting that studied measures to coordinate population development with economic and social development and heard a report on the implementation of the arrangements made at the national conference on the services sector. Noting that population is fundamental to a country's economic and social development, the meeting called for efforts to tap the demographic dividend and support high-quality economic and social development through high-quality population development. The meeting stressed the need to expand skills training and better align education and training with industrial development to promote high-quality and full employment. It also called for steady progress in ensuring equal access to basic public services and optimizing the infrastructure layout in line with population distribution. Efforts should be made to accelerate the development of a birth-friendly society and to maintain a stable number of newborns, according to the meeting. Regarding the service industry, the meeting emphasized its underpinning role in driving economic growth and called for stronger support in areas such as financing, land use, talent and data. The meeting urged continuous efforts to break down market access barriers, remove hidden hurdles for private investment, and explore innovative development paths tailored to local conditions. It also emphasized the need to increase investment in the services sector to unleash the potential of service consumption as well as cultivate leading enterprises and distinctive brands.

item.title: Xi calls for new achievements on new Long March
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
BEIJING, Oct. 22 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for new achievements on the new Long March as China commemorates the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March. "Only by remembering history can we create a brighter future," said Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, when addressing a gathering held in Beijing to mark the anniversary. Under Xi's proposal, all participants stood up and observed a moment of silence for the revolutionary heroes who gave their lives during the Long March and in revolutionary struggles across China. From October 1934 to October 1936, the Red Army marched through more than 10 provinces during the Long March, opening up a new chapter in the Chinese revolution, Xi said. "This earth-shattering revolutionary feat holds great significance in the history of our Party, country and military, and has a profound impact on our path toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," he noted. Xi stressed that the Party's right leadership and the establishment of Mao Zedong's core position were decisive for the victory of the Red Army's Long March. The Party and the Red Army relied on firm conviction, Xi said, adding that troops with noble ideals and firm beliefs are invincible. Xi emphasized the importance of integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities in addressing the country's issues and problems. He further underscored that the people will always be the source of strength and a strong support for the Party and the people's armed forces. Xi said the great spirit of the Long March demonstrates the power of loyalty, truth, justice and unity. "It will always be a precious treasure and a powerful driving force inspiring us to overcome difficulties and forge ahead courageously." He said the road of the Long March continues to extend. "On our new journey, we are now committed to realizing the Second Centenary Goal of building China into a great modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through a Chinese path to modernization," he said. To forge ahead on the new Long March, Xi said, it is imperative to stay committed to the Party's ideals, convictions and purpose and rely closely on the people to create new achievements. He underscored the need to unswervingly advance high-quality development and promote common prosperity for all. Efforts must be made to better ensure both development and security and seize the historical initiative to overcome difficulties, combat risks and meet challenges, he stressed. Xi also emphasized the importance of moving more quickly to reinforce the people's armed forces to world-class standards and adhering to the Party's absolute leadership over the military. It is also vital to uphold the leadership of the Party, strengthen Party building and persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance, he added. Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, as well as Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, attended the gathering. Zhao, who presided over the event, said Xi's speech was of immense political, ideological and guiding significance, urging earnest efforts to study and grasp its essence and ensure its effective implementation. He called on the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups to rally more closely around the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernization. Around 3,000 people participated in the gathering at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing.

item.title: Chinese vice premier meets foreign representatives attending International Science Council meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
BEIJING, Oct. 21 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang met with foreign representatives attending the 2026 International Science Council (ISC) Midterm Members' Meeting and Beijing Science Dialogue in Beijing on Wednesday. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said science and technology are the common wealth of humanity, and openness and cooperation are the inevitable choice for scientific and technological innovation. China stands ready to work with all parties to promote academic exchanges, tackle frontier scientific and technological challenges, produce scientific outcomes that benefit all, and jointly advance global science and technology, Ding said. ISC president Peter Gluckman and other foreign speakers commended China's achievements in scientific and technological innovation and expressed support for openness and cooperation, so that science can truly become a global public good and further contribute to human progress.

item.title: Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development Updated: October 16, 2026 18:55Xinhua ULANQAB, Inner Mongolia, Oct. 16 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded. During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area. He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner. Xi visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry. Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule. He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces. Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes.
